Indicator_Name: Emissions for five key air pollutants
Units_Measure: Index (2005=100); kilotonnes/year
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme A – Air; Indicator A1
Data_Source: National Atmospheric Emissions Inventory (NAEI); Defra Air Quality statistics
Climate_Rationale: Emissions modelled via NAEI activity data × emission factors; temperature affects NH3 volatilisation, but formal weather adjustment applies only to NH3. The NAEI uses meteorological data for deposition modelling components.

Indicator_Name: Emissions of greenhouse gases from natural resources, waste and fluorinated gases
Units_Measure: MtCO₂e/year
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Theme A – Air; Indicator A2
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory; National Atmospheric Emissions Inventory (NAEI)
Climate_Rationale: GHG emissions from natural resources and waste use IPCC inventory methods; temperature affects methane emissions from wetlands and permafrost (indirect).

Indicator_Name: Concentrations of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in the air
Units_Measure: µg/m³ (annual mean)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme A – Air; Indicator A3
Data_Source: Automatic Urban and Rural Network (AURN); Defra Air Quality statistics
Climate_Rationale: PM2.5 ambient concentrations directly measured by monitoring network; meteorological conditions (boundary layer height, wind speed, rainfall washout) are primary drivers of year-to-year variation in measured concentrations.

Indicator_Name: Rural background concentrations of ozone (O3)
Units_Measure: µg/m³ (annual mean / seasonal AOT40)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme A – Air; Indicator A4
Data_Source: Automatic Urban and Rural Network (AURN) rural ozone stations; Defra
Climate_Rationale: Rural ozone concentrations are strongly driven by temperature (photochemical production) and sunshine; ozone formation is directly dependent on weather variables.

Indicator_Name: Roadside nitrogen dioxide (NO2) concentrations
Units_Measure: µg/m³ (annual mean)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme A – Air; Indicator A5
Data_Source: Roadside air quality monitoring network (AURN); Local authority monitoring
Climate_Rationale: Roadside NO2 concentrations directly depend on wind speed, atmospheric stability and temperature; meteorological data underpin dispersion modelling used to interpret monitoring data.

Indicator_Name: Exceedance of damaging levels of nutrient nitrogen deposition on ecosystems
Units_Measure: % of ecosystem area in exceedance
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme A – Air; Indicator A6
Data_Source: CBED/FRAME atmospheric deposition model; CEH critical loads database
Climate_Rationale: Nutrient nitrogen deposition modelled via CBED/FRAME; rainfall directly determines wet deposition fraction — meteorological data are a direct model input.

Indicator_Name: Area of land exposed to damaging levels of ammonia (NH3) in the atmosphere
Units_Measure: % of land area above threshold
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme A – Air; Indicator A7
Data_Source: CBED/FRAME atmospheric deposition model; CEH ammonia mapping
Climate_Rationale: NH3 atmospheric exposure from dispersion modelling; temperature and wind speed directly affect volatilisation rates and dispersion — meteorological inputs are core to the model.

Indicator_Name: Pollution loads entering waters
Units_Measure: tonnes/year (nitrogen, phosphorus, sediment)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme B – Water; Indicator B1
Data_Source: EA Catchment Data; Water Framework Directive monitoring; Defra
Climate_Rationale: Pollution loads modelled from monitoring data and catchment models; river flow (directly climate-driven) determines diffuse load delivery — hydrological model inputs include rainfall.

Indicator_Name: Serious pollution incidents to water
Units_Measure: number of Category 1 & 2 incidents/year
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme B – Water; Indicator B2
Data_Source: Environment Agency National Incident Reporting System
Climate_Rationale: Pollution incidents from Environment Agency records; heavy rainfall (climate event) can trigger incidents but the indicator counts recorded events, not weather-adjusted.

Indicator_Name: State of the water environment
Units_Measure: % of water bodies in good/high ecological status (WFD)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems; Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme B – Water; Indicator B3
Data_Source: EA / NRW / SEPA Water Framework Directive classification assessments
Climate_Rationale: WFD ecological status; as for Biodiversity row 52 — temperature and low-flow conditions affect biological quality elements used in classification.

Indicator_Name: Condition of bathing waters
Units_Measure: % classified excellent or good
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme B – Water; Indicator B4
Data_Source: EA / SEPA / NRW bathing water classification assessments
Climate_Rationale: Bathing water quality from in-season sampling; rainfall events cause CSO overflows affecting quality but the indicator reports classification results.

Indicator_Name: Water bodies achieving sustainable abstraction criteria
Units_Measure: % of water bodies meeting criteria
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: Theme B – Water; Indicator B5
Data_Source: EA Water Framework Directive abstraction assessment
Climate_Rationale: Sustainable abstraction from licence compliance monitoring; low flows (drought) affect whether criteria are met but the indicator reports compliance status.

Indicator_Name: Natural functions of water and wetland ecosystems
Units_Measure: index / area (ha) of functional floodplain and wetland
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: Theme B – Water; Indicator B6
Data_Source: Environment Agency; Countryside Survey (CEH); wetland habitat monitoring
Climate_Rationale: Natural functions of wetland ecosystems assessed via hydrological condition indicators; rainfall and water table (climate variables) directly determine wetland function scores.

Indicator_Name: Health of freshwaters assessed through fish populations
Units_Measure: % of river length in good or high status (WFD fish index)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species; Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme B – Water; Indicator B7
Data_Source: EA / NRW / SEPA fish population surveys (WFD fish index)
Climate_Rationale: Fish population WFD index includes temperature-sensitive species; electrofishing surveys may be affected by water temperature and flow conditions.

Indicator_Name: Clean seas: marine litter
Units_Measure: items per 100m of shoreline; items per km² seabed
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C1
Data_Source: Marine Conservation Society beach litter surveys; MMO seabed surveys; OSPAR
Climate_Rationale: Marine litter from beach/seabed survey counts; storm events (climate) affect litter deposition but surveys are standardised and not weather-adjusted.

Indicator_Name: Seabed subject to high pressure from human activity
Units_Measure: % of seabed area
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable use of wild species; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C2
Data_Source: MMO vessel monitoring system (VMS); ICES trawling pressure data
Climate_Rationale: Seabed pressure from fishing effort data; storm frequency (climate) affects fishing access but the indicator primarily tracks effort from vessel monitoring data.

Indicator_Name: Diverse seas: status of marine mammals and marine birds
Units_Measure: index of abundance / population trend
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C3
Data_Source: JNCC / ICES; Joint Cetacean Protocol; Seabird Monitoring Programme (SMP)
Climate_Rationale: Marine mammal and seabird status from monitoring programmes; sea surface temperature affects prey availability, a key driver of population trends.

Indicator_Name: Diverse seas: condition of seafloor habitats
Units_Measure: % of seafloor habitats in good condition
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C4
Data_Source: Marine Biodiversity Monitoring Programme (MBMP); JNCC; Natural England
Climate_Rationale: Seafloor habitat condition from MBMP surveys; physical disturbance from storms affects habitat condition but survey methodology does not formally weather-correct.

Indicator_Name: Diverse seas: condition of pelagic habitats
Units_Measure: index of plankton community state
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C5
Data_Source: Continuous Plankton Recorder (CPR) Survey; SAHFOS / MBA
Climate_Rationale: Pelagic habitat condition assessed via plankton community state indices; sea temperature and stratification (both climate variables) are the primary drivers of plankton community composition.

Indicator_Name: Diverse seas: status of threatened and declining features
Units_Measure: % of threatened/declining features at target condition
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C6
Data_Source: JNCC MPA monitoring; country nature conservation bodies feature condition data
Climate_Rationale: Threatened/declining feature status from conservation assessments; climate change is a recognised threat but condition assessments are based on field surveys.

Indicator_Name: Healthy seas: fish and shellfish populations
Units_Measure: % of assessed stocks at or above biomass reference point
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable use of wild species
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C7
Data_Source: ICES stock assessments; Marine Management Organisation (MMO) fisheries data
Climate_Rationale: Fish and shellfish population status from ICES stock assessments; SST embedded in stock recruitment models.

Indicator_Name: Healthy seas: marine food webs functioning
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries | Land Use & Agriculture
Units_Measure: mean trophic level of landings; plankton index
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Ecosystem integrity
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C8
Data_Source: CPR Survey; ICES mean trophic level of commercial fish landings; MMO
Climate_Rationale: Marine food web functioning via mean trophic level of landings and plankton indices; SST directly drives plankton phenology and fish diet composition — temperature is a core explanatory variable.

Indicator_Name: Healthy seas: seafloor habitats functioning
Units_Measure: % of seafloor habitats functionally intact
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Ecosystem integrity; Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C9
Data_Source: JNCC benthic habitat condition surveys; OSPAR seafloor integrity data
Climate_Rationale: Seafloor functioning from survey data; temperature affects benthic community metabolism and recovery rates.

Indicator_Name: Productive seas: fish and shellfish stocks fished sustainably
Units_Measure: % of stocks fished at or below FMSY
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable use of wild species
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C10
Data_Source: ICES stock assessments; MMO fisheries statistics
Climate_Rationale: Fish stocks at FMSY from ICES assessments; climate embedded in recruitment and growth parameters.

Indicator_Name: Status of sensitive fish species
Units_Measure: index of abundance for elasmobranch species
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species; Sustainable use of wild species
Source_Reference: Theme C – Seas & Estuaries; Indicator C11
Data_Source: ICES North Sea and Celtic Sea trawl surveys (IBTS); Marine Scotland
Climate_Rationale: Sensitive fish species (elasmobranch) abundance index; bottom temperature affects distribution and catchability in trawl surveys.

Indicator_Name: Quantity, quality and connectivity of habitats
Units_Measure: area (ha) and connectivity index of semi-natural habitat
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Source_Reference: Theme D – Wildlife; Indicator D1
Data_Source: Countryside Survey (CEH); Priority Habitat Inventory (Natural England); JNCC
Climate_Rationale: Habitat quantity, quality and connectivity from Countryside Survey and remote sensing; climate is a long-term driver but not a direct input to extent/connectivity calculations.

Indicator_Name: Extent and condition of protected sites – land, water and sea
Units_Measure: % of SSSI / MPA area in favourable or recovering condition
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Source_Reference: Theme D – Wildlife; Indicator D2
Data_Source: Natural England SSSI condition monitoring; JNCC MPA condition data
Climate_Rationale: Protected site condition from SSSI assessments; as for Biodiversity row 29.

Indicator_Name: Area of woodland in England
Units_Measure: thousand hectares; % land cover
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Source_Reference: Theme D – Wildlife; Indicator D3
Data_Source: Forestry Commission / Forest Research National Forest Inventory
Climate_Rationale: Woodland area from Forestry Commission inventory; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Relative abundance and/or distribution of species
Units_Measure: multi-taxon abundance index (index, baseline=100)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: Theme D – Wildlife; Indicator D4
Data_Source: BTO Breeding Bird Survey; UKBMS; NBN Atlas occupancy models (CEH/JNCC)
Climate_Rationale: Species abundance/distribution index; aggregates monitoring data including weather-sensitive taxa (birds, butterflies, bats).

Indicator_Name: Conservation status of our native species
Units_Measure: % of species assessments in favourable status
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: Theme D – Wildlife; Indicator D5
Data_Source: IUCN Red List assessments; JNCC / country NCBs species assessments
Climate_Rationale: Conservation status (EPC C equivalent); Red List Index based partly on climate-driven range changes.

Indicator_Name: Relative abundance and distribution of priority species in England
Units_Measure: index of abundance for priority species
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: Theme D – Wildlife; Indicator D6
Data_Source: Multi-species recording schemes; NBN Atlas; CEH occupancy models
Climate_Rationale: Priority species relative abundance; as for JNCC row 25 — multi-taxon index including weather-sensitive groups.

Indicator_Name: Species supporting ecosystem functions
Units_Measure: index of functionally important species (pollinators, decomposers, predators)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Ecosystem integrity; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: Theme D – Wildlife; Indicator D7
Data_Source: UKBMS (pollinators); BTO BBS (insectivorous birds); Rothamsted (invertebrates)
Climate_Rationale: Species supporting ecosystem functions includes pollinators; PoMS pollinator counts are weather-sensitive.

Indicator_Name: Area of productive agricultural land
Units_Measure: thousand hectares by land grade
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E1
Data_Source: Agricultural Land Classification survey; Defra / ONS farm structure
Climate_Rationale: Agricultural land area by grade from classification surveys; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Volume of agricultural production
Units_Measure: index of crop and livestock output (index, baseline=100)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E2
Data_Source: Defra Agricultural Output Price Index; ONS farm accounts
Climate_Rationale: Agricultural output volume index; weather strongly affects yields but the indicator uses production statistics without formal weather adjustment.

Indicator_Name: Volume of inputs used in agricultural production
Units_Measure: index of fertiliser, pesticide, energy inputs (index)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels; Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E3
Data_Source: British Survey of Fertiliser Practice (BSFP); Defra pesticide usage statistics
Climate_Rationale: Agricultural input volumes (fertiliser, pesticide, energy) from surveys; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Efficiency of agricultural production measured by Total Factor Productivity
Units_Measure: Total Factor Productivity index
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E4
Data_Source: Defra Agricultural Total Factor Productivity Index (economic modelling)
Climate_Rationale: Total Factor Productivity index; weather affects output in any given year but TFP calculation uses economic modelling without formal weather correction.

Indicator_Name: Percentage of annual growth of trees in English woodlands that is harvested
Units_Measure: % of annual increment harvested
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E5
Data_Source: Forestry Commission Timber Production statistics
Climate_Rationale: Proportion of annual woodland increment harvested from Forestry Commission data; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Volume of timber brought to market per annum from English sources
Units_Measure: thousand green tonnes/year
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E6
Data_Source: Forestry Commission / Forest Research timber market statistics
Climate_Rationale: Timber volume from market statistics; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Healthy soils
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Health
Units_Measure: % of soils in good condition (organic matter, structure, biology)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems; Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E7
Data_Source: Countryside Survey (CEH) soil monitoring; National Soil Monitoring Network (NSMN)
Climate_Rationale: Healthy soils index; temperature and rainfall affect organic matter decomposition and soil biology but survey data are not weather-adjusted.

Indicator_Name: Efficient use of water
Units_Measure: megalitres/day abstracted; leakage rate (Ml/d)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E8
Data_Source: EA / Ofwat water abstraction and leakage statistics; WRMP data
Climate_Rationale: Efficient water use from abstraction and leakage data; drought years naturally reduce availability and efficiency metrics but indicator uses reported data.

Indicator_Name: Percentage of our seafood coming from healthy ecosystems, produced sustainably
Units_Measure: % of seafood from certified or sustainably assessed sources
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustainable use of wild species
Source_Reference: Theme E – Natural Resources; Indicator E9
Data_Source: ICES stock assessments; MMO; MSC certification data
Climate_Rationale: Seafood sustainability from ICES stock assessments; SST embedded in stock models as for Biodiversity row 130.

Indicator_Name: Disruption or unwanted impacts from flooding or coastal erosion
Units_Measure: number of properties flooded; hectares eroded
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Theme F – Resilience; Indicator F1
Data_Source: EA Flood Risk Management reporting; National Flood Risk Assessment (NaFRA)
Climate_Rationale: Flooding and coastal erosion impacts are directly driven by extreme rainfall events, storm surge and sea level rise; all are climate/weather variables. The indicator measures climate-driven impacts directly.

Indicator_Name: Communities resilient to flooding and coastal erosion
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries | Governance, Society & Data
Units_Measure: number of properties better protected; flood risk management outcomes
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Theme F – Resilience; Indicator F2
Data_Source: EA Flood and Coastal Risk Management national outcome measures
Climate_Rationale: Flood resilience measures (properties protected); targets are set partly based on climate change projections and flood risk modelling using climate scenarios.

Indicator_Name: Disruption or unwanted impacts caused by drought
Units_Measure: drought impact index; days of drought restriction
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: Theme F – Resilience; Indicator F3
Data_Source: EA / SEPA / NRW drought impact assessments; Defra drought monitoring
Climate_Rationale: Drought impacts are directly caused by rainfall deficits and high evapotranspiration (temperature-driven); the indicator explicitly measures climate-driven disruption.

Indicator_Name: Changes in landscape and waterscape character
Units_Measure: index of landscape character change
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustaining nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: Theme G – Natural Beauty & Engagement; Indicator G1
Data_Source: Natural England / Historic England landscape character change assessments
Climate_Rationale: Landscape character change from condition surveys; climate change is a recognised driver of landscape change (vegetation shifts, coastal erosion) but surveys do not formally use climate data.

Indicator_Name: Condition of heritage features including designated geological sites and scheduled monuments
Units_Measure: % of designated features in satisfactory condition
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Sustaining nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: Theme G – Natural Beauty & Engagement; Indicator G2
Data_Source: Historic England; JNCC; Natural England designated geological sites data
Climate_Rationale: Heritage feature condition from inspection records; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Enhancement of green and blue infrastructure
Units_Measure: area (ha) of new or improved green/blue infrastructure
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Green and blue spaces in urban areas
Source_Reference: Theme G – Natural Beauty & Engagement; Indicator G3
Data_Source: Defra / Natural England green infrastructure programme reporting
Climate_Rationale: Green/blue infrastructure enhancement from project reporting; weather is background factor affecting vegetation establishment but not used in calculation.

Indicator_Name: Engagement with the natural environment
Units_Measure: % of adults visiting natural environments weekly
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Participation and rights of indigenous peoples
Source_Reference: Theme G – Natural Beauty & Engagement; Indicator G4
Data_Source: Natural England Monitor of Engagement with the Natural Environment (MENE)
Climate_Rationale: Engagement with natural environment from survey data; visit frequency is weather-sensitive but surveys use annual data without weather correction.

Indicator_Name: People engaged in social action for the environment
Units_Measure: number of participants in environmental volunteering
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Participation and rights of indigenous peoples
Source_Reference: Theme G – Natural Beauty & Engagement; Indicator G5
Data_Source: NCVO; Wildlife Trusts; RSPB; National Trust volunteering records
Climate_Rationale: Environmental volunteering from organisational records; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Environmental attitudes and behaviours
Units_Measure: % of adults with positive environmental attitudes/behaviours (survey index)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Knowledge and data for decision-making; Participation and rights of indigenous peoples
Source_Reference: Theme G – Natural Beauty & Engagement; Indicator G6
Data_Source: Defra Public Attitudes and Behaviours Tracker (PABT)
Climate_Rationale: Environmental attitudes from survey data; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Health and wellbeing benefits
Units_Measure: % of adults reporting wellbeing benefits from nature contact
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) — 2030 Agenda; Sustaining nature's contributions to people; UN SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being)
Source_Reference: Theme G – Natural Beauty & Engagement; Indicator G7
Data_Source: Natural England MENE wellbeing module; People and Nature Survey (PANS)
Climate_Rationale: Health and wellbeing benefits from nature contact from survey data; outdoor activity is weather-sensitive but surveys use annual averages.

Indicator_Name: Abatement of the number of invasive non-native species entering and establishing
Units_Measure: number of new INNS establishing per year vs baseline
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Eliminate and control invasive alien species
Source_Reference: Theme H – Biosecurity, Chemical & Noise; Indicator H1
Data_Source: GB Non-Native Species Information Portal (NNSIP); JNCC
Climate_Rationale: INNS establishment rate; climate warming facilitates establishment of many INNS but counts are from species databases, not formally weather-adjusted.

Indicator_Name: Distribution of invasive non-native species and plant pests and diseases
Units_Measure: area (ha) or number of records of INNS
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Eliminate and control invasive alien species
Source_Reference: Theme H – Biosecurity, Chemical & Noise; Indicator H2
Data_Source: GB NNSIP; CEH species range data; Forestry Commission pest distribution maps
Climate_Rationale: INNS distribution; as above — climate is a facilitating factor for range expansion.

Indicator_Name: Emissions of mercury and persistent organic pollutants to the environment
Units_Measure: kg/year (mercury); index (POPs)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme H – Biosecurity, Chemical & Noise; Indicator H3
Data_Source: NAEI heavy metals and POP inventory; EA environmental monitoring
Climate_Rationale: Mercury and POP emissions from inventories; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Exposure and adverse effects of chemicals on wildlife in the environment
Units_Measure: concentration index in biota; % of species above threshold
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme H – Biosecurity, Chemical & Noise; Indicator H4
Data_Source: EA / SEPA / NRW chemical monitoring; Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH)
Climate_Rationale: Chemical exposure to wildlife from monitoring; temperature affects chemical mobility and toxicity in the environment but monitoring data are not temperature-adjusted.

Indicator_Name: Exposure to transport noise
Units_Measure: number of people exposed to >55dB Lden transport noise
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme H – Biosecurity, Chemical & Noise; Indicator H5
Data_Source: Defra / DfT strategic noise mapping (Environmental Noise Regulations 2006)
Climate_Rationale: Transport noise exposure from modelling; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Carbon footprint and consumer buying choices
Units_Measure: tCO₂e/capita (consumption-based); % choosing low-carbon options
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: Theme J – Resource Use & Waste; Indicator J1
Data_Source: Defra / ONS UK consumption-based emissions statistics; CarbonBrief/BEIS data
Climate_Rationale: Carbon footprint of consumption from input-output analysis; climate slightly affects energy use for heating/cooling but consumption data are not weather-adjusted.

Indicator_Name: Raw material consumption
Units_Measure: tonnes/capita domestic material consumption
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Business assessment and disclosure of biodiversity; Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: Theme J – Resource Use & Waste; Indicator J2
Data_Source: ONS UK Domestic Material Consumption accounts; Defra resource statistics
Climate_Rationale: Raw material consumption from economic accounts; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Municipal waste recycling rates
Units_Measure: % of municipal waste recycled
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: Theme J – Resource Use & Waste; Indicator J3
Data_Source: DEFRA / EA municipal waste statistics; local authority waste data
Climate_Rationale: Waste recycling rates from EA statistics; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Residual waste arising by type and sector
Units_Measure: million tonnes/year residual waste
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: Theme J – Resource Use & Waste; Indicator J4
Data_Source: EA / Defra waste surveys and commercial/industrial waste statistics
Climate_Rationale: Residual waste from statistics; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Prevent harmful chemicals from being recycled
Units_Measure: % of recycled material free from substances of concern
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: Theme J – Resource Use & Waste; Indicator J5
Data_Source: EA chemicals in products and waste monitoring; ECHA data
Climate_Rationale: Harmful chemicals in recycled materials from compliance monitoring; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Waste crime
Units_Measure: number / volume of illegal waste sites and fly-tipping incidents
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: Theme J – Resource Use & Waste; Indicator J6
Data_Source: EA fly-tipping statistics; EA illegal waste site enforcement data
Climate_Rationale: Waste crime incidents from enforcement records; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Global environmental impacts of UK consumption of key commodities
Units_Measure: deforestation risk index (ha equivalent) from UK imports
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Business assessment and disclosure of biodiversity; Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: Theme K – International; Indicator K1
Data_Source: Global Environmental Impacts of Consumption (GEIC) model; Trase trade data
Climate_Rationale: Global deforestation footprint of UK consumption; drought and fire (climate-driven) contribute to tropical deforestation in supply chains but the IOTA model uses trade and land-use data primarily.

Indicator_Name: Developing countries better able to protect and improve the environment with UK support
Units_Measure: number of countries supported; ODA spend (£ million)
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Mobilise USD 200bn/year for biodiversity
Source_Reference: Theme K – International; Indicator K2
Data_Source: FCDO international development ODA statistics (Rio Markers); OECD DAC
Climate_Rationale: ODA for developing-country environment protection from financial records; no climate data.

Indicator_Name: Status of endemic and globally threatened species in the UK Overseas Territories
Units_Measure: Red List Index for UK Overseas Territory endemic species
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: Theme K – International; Indicator K3
Data_Source: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species; JNCC UKOT biodiversity programme
Climate_Rationale: Red List Index for UK Overseas Territory species; as for Biodiversity row 82 — climate change is a key driver embedded in IUCN threat assessments.

Indicator_Name: Extent and condition of terrestrial and marine protected areas in the UK Overseas Territories
Units_Measure: % of land and sea area protected; % in good condition
Policy_Goal: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025; Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF); 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Source_Reference: Theme K – International; Indicator K4
Data_Source: JNCC UKOT protected areas GIS; country conservation agencies
Climate_Rationale: Extent and condition of UKOTs protected areas from survey/designation data; no climate data in area calculation.
